He played college basketball for [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]]. He played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[NBA]] in 2016–18. ==High school career== Whitehead began his basketball career playing for [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn)|Abraham Lincoln High School]], and was recruited by a number of college programs. Whitehead played at the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], the 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and other major tournaments in high school. He was labeled a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and [[247Sports.com]], being named [[Mr. New York Basketball]], the recipient of the 2014 PSAL Wingate Award, Co-Most Valuable Player in the 2013 Under Armour Elite 24 game, and the highest-rated New York City recruit since 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.shupirates.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/isaiah_whitehead_911979.html |title=Isaiah Whitehead Bio |work=SHUPirates.com |access-date=October 1, 2014 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006071222/http://www.shupirates.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/isaiah_whitehead_911979.html |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }} ==College career== Whitehead was named preseason Big East Rookie of the Year and made the All-Rookie Team as a freshman. He was twice selected as Rookie of the Week on December 8 and December 15. He missed nine games during the season due to a stress fracture in his right foot. At the conclusion of the 2015–16 regular season, Whitehead was unanimously selected to the All-Big East first team.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2016/3/6/MBB_0306160917.aspx|title=Four Named Unanimously to MBB All-BIG EAST First Team|work=BigEast.com|date=March 6, 2016|access-date=March 6, 2016}} He also received the [[Haggerty Award]], given to the New York area's top men's Division I basketball player.{{cite web|first=Jerry|last=Carino|url=http://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2016/04/12/seton-halls-whitehead-wins-haggerty-award/82924738/|title=Seton Hall's Whitehead wins Haggerty Award|work=App.com|date=April 12, 2016|access-date=April 12, 2016}} Whitehead led Seton Hall to their first Big East Championship in 23 years. The Pirates took down Creighton, Xavier and Villanova in the final. Whitehead was awarded with the Tournament's Most Outstanding Player award. Next, the Hall earned their first NCAA berth in 10 years. Seton Hall was defeated by the Gonzaga Bulldogs in the first round in Denver. In March 2016, Whitehead declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/03/18/seton-hall-isaiah-whitehead-nba-draft|title=Seton Hall's Isaiah Whitehead to enter NBA draft, will not hire agent|work=SI.com|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=March 18, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets (2016–2018)=== On June 23, 2016, Whitehead was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 42nd overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He was later traded to his hometown team the [[Brooklyn Nets]] the following day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/06/24/brooklyn-nets-acquire-draft-rights-isaiah-whitehead|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Draft Rights to Isaiah Whitehead|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=June 24, 2016}} On July 8, 2016, he signed with the Nets and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/07/08/brooklyn-nets-sign-isaiah-whitehead|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Isaiah Whitehead|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}} On January 6, 2017, Whitehead recorded his first career [[double-double]] with 10 points and 10 rebounds in 116–108 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|last=Logan|first=Greg|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/spencer-dinwiddie-trying-to-make-best-of-his-shot-with-nets-d29905|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220092745/http://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/spencer-dinwiddie-trying-to-make-best-of-his-shot-with-nets-1.12887095|url-status=live|archive-date=February 20, 2017|title=Spencer Dinwiddie trying to make best of his shot with Nets|work=NewsDay.com|date=January 7, 2017|access-date=February 19, 2017}} On March 10, 2017, he scored a career-high 24 points in a 105–96 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900366|title=Nowitzki, sluggish Mavs put away Nets 105–96 after 30K night|work=ESPN.com|date=March 10, 2017|access-date=March 11, 2017}} On April 8, 2017, with one block against the [[Chicago Bulls]], Whitehead tied an all-time team record by a guard in a single-season with 36, set by [[Darwin Cook]] during the 1980–81 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900566|title=Wade returns but Nets hand Bulls potentially costly loss|work=ESPN.com|date=April 8, 2017|access-date=April 8, 2017}} On November 27, 2017, Whitehead tied his career high with 24 points while shooting 10 of 16 from the field in a 117–103 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975045|title=Harden helps Rockets beat Nets 117–103|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2017|access-date=November 27, 2017}} During the 2017–18 season, he was assigned multiple times to the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2017–18 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 27, 2017}} He was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] and later waived.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/arthur-faried-traded-to-nets-071318|title=Denver Nuggets Trade Arthur and Faried to Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018|quote=Denver will subsequently waived{{sic}} Whitehead.}} In 30 games of the 2017–18 NBA G League season, Whitehead averaged 22.3 PPG, 3.7 RPG and 3.6 APG in 28.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1627785/|title=Isaiah Whitehead |website=NBA G League Stats}} ===Lokomotiv Kuban (2018–2019)=== Whitehead signed with the Russian team [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] on August 6, 2018.{{cite web |title=Lokomotiv Kuban signs Isaiah Whitehead |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/russia/284796/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-isaiah-whitehead.html |website=Sportando |access-date=August 6, 2018 |archive-date=August 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806180146/https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/russia/284796/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-isaiah-whitehead.html |url-status=dead }} He averaged 11.3 points, club|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/isaiah-whitehead-parts-ways-with-russian-club/|website=CBS Sports|access-date=January 15, 2019|date=January 7, 2019}} === Grand Rapids Drive (2019) === On January 15, 2019, Whitehead signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]] on a two-way contract.{{cite web|title=Pistons sign guards Kalin Lucas, Isaiah Whitehead|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2019/01/15/report-detroit-pistons-sign-point-guard-isaiah-whitehead/2581430002/|website=[[The Detroit News]]|access-date=January 16, 2019|date= January 15, 2019}} He did not end up appearing in any games for the Pistons. In four games of the 2018–19 NBA G League season, Whitehead has averaged 19.5 PPG, 4.5 RPG and 6.3 APG in 33.8 minutes per game. On June 23, 2019, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] signed Whitehead to their Summer League roster.{{cite web|title=Blazers Add Point Guard Isaiah Whitehead to Summer League Squad|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2019/6/23/18714884/trail-blazers-summer-league-roster-isaiah-whitehead-signed|website=[[SB Nation]]|access-date=July 11, 2019|date=June 23, 2019}} === BC Astana (2019) === On October 10, 2019, Whitehead signed with [[BC Astana]] of the [[Kazakhstan Basketball Championship|Kazakhstan Championship]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/astana-tabs-isaiah-whitehead/|title=Astana tabs Isaiah Whitehead|date=October 10, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 11, 2019|last1=Borghesan|first1=Ennio Terrasi|archive-date=February 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222162834/https://sportando.basketball/en/astana-tabs-isaiah-whitehead/|url-status=dead}} In five games, he averaged 9.6 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=John |title=Isaiah Whitehead joins Mornar Bar |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1009835/isaiah-whitehead-joins-mornar-bar/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=July 18, 2020 |date=January 25, 2020}} ===Mornar Bar (2020–2021)=== On January 25, 2020, Whitehead signed with [[KK Mornar Bar|Mornar Bar]] of the [[ABA League]] and [[Montenegrin Basketball League|Montenegrin League]]. He played five games before the season was suspended, scoring 24 points in his only Champions League appearance. On April 29, he extended his contract with the team.{{cite news |title=Isaiah Whitehead to extend with KK Mornar Bar |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/isaiah-whitehead-to-extend-with-kk-mornar-bar/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 18, 2020 |date=April 29, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Beşiktaş (2021–2022)=== On August 27, 2021, Whitehead signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] of the [[Basketball Super League]].{{cite news |title=Beşiktaş officially signs Isaiah Whitehead |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/besiktas-officially-signs-isaiah-whitehead/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 27, 2021 |date=August 27, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} He averaged 11.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game. === Riesen Ludwigsburg (2022–2023)=== On September 23, 2022, he has signed with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg-lands-isaiah-whitehead/|title=MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg lands Isaiah Whitehead|date=September 23, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 24, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} Whitehead and Ludwigsburg parted ways on January 15, 2023, the contract was mutually cancelled.{{cite web|url=https://mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/news/vertragsaufloesung-isaiah-whitehead/|title=Vertragsauflösung Isaiah Whitehead |website=MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg}} === Beşiktaş (2023)=== On January 17, 2023, he signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K.
